deep.reconstruction:
The page has three independent jottings.

(A) Counting products of two primes. Heading: 'Bestimmung der Zahl der Primzahlproducte pq welche < n sind', i.e. estimate N_2(n) = #{p*q < n : p, q prime}. The only formula written is an auxiliary product f(n) = 2^n n! * 2^(n/2) (n/2)! * ... * 2^0 (n/n)!. The intended reading is presumably f(n) = prod_{k=1}^{n} c_k * [n/k]!, with 'n/k' meaning floor(n/k).

The previous page explains the context. There Hilbert works with Chebyshev's functions T(x) = log [x]! and psi(x), and with the inequality f(x) < psi(x) < f(2x) for f(x) = T(x) - 2T(x/2). So this page is a Chebyshev-type attempt one level up: from primes to semiprimes.

The underlying identity (my addition, standard) is log [x]! = sum_{m<=x} psi(x/m) = sum_{j<=x} Lambda(j) [x/j]. Taking the log of a product of factorials [n/k]! gives sum_k T(n/k) = sum_k sum_m psi(n/(k m)) = sum_{j<=n} Lambda(j) D(n/j), where D(x) = sum_{m<=x} d(m) is the divisor summatory function.

Weighted products of this type generate Dirichlet convolutions of Lambda with arithmetic functions. Combinations like Lambda*Lambda, or sums of psi(n/p) over primes, are what control sum_{pq<n} log p log q, and hence N_2(n) ~ n log log n / log n (Landau 1900).

The factors 2^(n/k) are not explained. Their exponents (n, n/2, ..., and then 0 instead of the expected n/n = 1) do not fit a clean pattern. No derivation follows, so the computation is a fragmentary programme, not a result.

(B) Philosophy of number. 'Die Zahl ist der fingirte, gedachte Träger einer Regel, oder ein wandernder Schnitt': a (real) number is the fictitious carrier of a rule, i.e. of a Cauchy/Cantor fundamental sequence, or a 'wandering cut', i.e. a Dedekind cut. Practically we represent such a carrier as a point: negative numbers to the left, imaginary numbers perpendicular (the Argand/Gauss plane).

(C) Continuity axiom. To pass from the concept of number to the concept of magnitude in geometric intuition, one needs only one axiom. The totality of numbers (rational and irrational) can be mapped onto a curve, generated by the motion of a point, so that:
- each number corresponds to exactly one point and conversely (a bijection R <-> curve);
- if a > b, the pair corresponds to the direction alpha-beta;
- if c < d, the pair corresponds to the opposite direction beta-alpha.
In modern terms: there is an order-preserving (or order-reversing) bijection between R and the points of a line or arc. This is the Cantor–Dedekind axiom.
errors: The product f(n) is not internally consistent as written: the exponents of 2 run n, n/2, ..., but the last factor is written 2^0 instead of 2^(n/n) = 2^1. Either the pattern is different from what the visible terms suggest, or it is a slip.
Nothing is derived about the count of products pq. The relation between f(n) and the number of semiprimes is not stated, so no step can be verified.

In (C) the order condition is stated loosely: 'a > b corresponds to direction alpha-beta'. Strictly this needs monotonicity for all pairs, which is what is clearly meant. Hilbert also does not address whether such a correspondence requires a completeness property of the curve; he simply posits it as an axiom, which is legitimate.

results.what: Programme to estimate the number of products of two primes below n via a Chebyshev-type product of factorials [n/k]!
results.modern_name: Chebyshev's method for semiprimes / counting function pi_2(x) of almost-primes
results.usually_credited_to: Chebyshev (1850s) for the method; asymptotic for pi_2 by Landau (1900)

results.what: Real number as carrier of a rule (fundamental sequence) or as a 'wandering cut'
results.modern_name: Cantor/Méray construction of reals via Cauchy sequences; Dedekind cuts

results.what: Geometric representation: negatives to the left, imaginaries perpendicular
results.modern_name: Number line and Argand/Gauss complex plane

results.what: Single axiom of an order-preserving bijection between the reals and the points of a curve, to pass from number to geometric magnitude
results.modern_name: Cantor–Dedekind axiom (continuity axiom); precursor of Hilbert's Vollständigkeitsaxiom
results.usually_credited_to: Cantor (1872) and Dedekind (1872); Hilbert's completeness axiom in Grundlagen der Geometrie (2nd ed. 1903, Festschrift 1900 addition)

deep.surprise_reason: Everything on the page is standard for the 1880s. The prime-count note is an unexecuted Chebyshev-style idea. The number-concept remarks restate Cantor/Dedekind. The continuity axiom is an early private anticipation of Hilbert's later, well-known completeness axiom, and his early interest in foundations is documented (e.g. by Toepell). This gives modest biographical interest but no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: n=30; sp.simplify(sp.log(sp.factorial(n)) - sum(sp.floor(n/p**k)*sp.log(p) for p in sp.primerange(2,n+1) for k in range(1,6))) == 0
checkable.asserts: Legendre/Chebyshev identity: log n! = sum_{p^k<=n} floor(n/p^k) log p = sum_j Lambda(j) floor(n/j), the basis of T(x) = log [x]!

checkable.sympy: len([m for m in range(2,100) if sum(sp.factorint(m).values())==2]) == 34
checkable.asserts: There are 34 products pq (p <= q prime) below 100, which is the quantity the page sets out to count.

checkable.asserts: log prod_k [n/k]! = sum_{j<=n} Lambda(j) * D(n/j), with D the divisor summatory function: the analytic content of a product of the type f(n) without the 2-power weights.

Formula line: the factors are best read as 2^n n!, 2^(n/2) (n/2)!, ..., 2^0 (n/n)!, with (n/k)! presumably meaning [n/k]!. The final exponent really appears as 0 in the image.
